newsitem.title: UK: UK to look at speeding up immigrant deportations.
newsitem.headline: UK to look at speeding up immigrant deportations.

text.p: Britain's new Labour government is looking at ways of speeding up the process of deporting immigrants deemed to be illegal or refused asylum, the Home Office said on Monday.

"When we make a decision not to allow someone to remain in this country and that case has no special compassionate circumstances, then it should be enforced," junior Home Office (interior) minister Mike O'Brien said in a statement.

O'Brien said the previous Conservative government, ousted by Labour in an election last month, had failed to carry out deportation orders against thousands of people who had not met strict immigration criteria over the past 18 years.
"The Tories (Conservatives) talked tough but failed to act firmly. Ministers were not prepared to ensure that their own policy was carried out," he said.
The Daily Telegraph newspaper said the new government was planning to deport some 50,000 illegal immigrants and bogus asylum seekers in a drive to enforce deportation orders.

The newspaper said that despite a doubling in the number of deportation orders signed under tough new rules introduced by the Conservatives in 1993, the number of people actually removed from the country had fallen substantially over the past five years.
The Home Office said the figure of 50,000 proposed deportations was speculative.
